CHRW.thesis_one_line: America's biggest freight-booking middleman is earning more per dollar of gross profit through automation, but the price already assumes a strong freight recovery and a $604 million jury verdict hangs over it.
kill_criteria: Adjusted gross profit per NAST truckload shipment falls year-over-year for two consecutive quarters while NAST volume growth trails the Cass Freight Shipment Index (market-share thesis broken; source: quarterly earnings release NAST table).

Consolidated debt (10-Q debt footnote: revolver + receivables securitization + senior notes, carrying value) exceeds 2.5x trailing-twelve-month adjusted EBITDA, versus about 1.6x at 30 Jun 2026 (Yahoo-derived EBITDA, cross-check only).

Lipe v. Lupus Superior (Dallas County) is entered as a final judgment of $300 million or more against C.H. Robinson and is not stayed or bonded within insurance limits, or a settlement/accrual above the $155 million per-occurrence insurance tower is disclosed.

Quarterly adjusted diluted EPS (non-GAAP, release reconciliation) is below $1.25 in any quarter of 2027, i.e. no step-up from the Q4 2025 level of $1.23 (earnings power not rising despite claimed productivity gains).

Net cash from operating activities (10-Q cash flow statement, consolidated) is below $250 million for full-year 2026, meaning the working-capital build is not reversing while buybacks and dividends continue to be debt-funded.
key_adverse_facts: Lipe v. Lupus Superior jury verdict of 23 July 2026: total damages $604 million, C.H. Robinson allocated 23% but possibly jointly and severally liable for the full amount; insurance $155 million per occurrence with $5 million deductible (10-Q Note 7, filed 2026-07-31); no reasonable estimate of loss beyond an immaterial accrual.

Q2 2026 cash from operations fell to $35.9 million (from $227.1 million) while $301.3 million was returned to shareholders; long-term debt rose to $1,685.0 million from $1,089.4 million in six months (consolidated balance sheet).

Adjusted gross profit grew only 6.5% in Q2 2026 (to $738.0 million) and fell 1.9% in Q1 2026; earnings growth is mostly cost removal (headcount down 10.8%) and freight-cycle pricing, and Global Forwarding adjusted gross profit is down 5.7% year to date.
Stock at $147.10 is 19.6x Yahoo forward EPS of $7.50 and 26x trailing adjusted EPS of $5.59, and the company gives no numeric earnings guidance.
data_conflicts: Yahoo trailing free cash flow $480.6 million vs 10-Q-derived TTM OCF less capex and software of about $618 million (Yahoo appears to net other investing items; filings used).
Q08 triage had an empty red_flags list; the Lipe verdict (filed 10-Q 2026-07-31) was not reflected. b1 rank 238 (composite 0.52) is mid-table; triage quality/growth 3/3 not overturned.
CHRW.next_earnings_date: 2026-10-28 (estimated from prior-year pattern, release of 2025-10-29; company confirmation not checked)
CHRW.confidence_in_thesis: low-med: cost execution is verified in filings, but freight-cycle dependency and the Lipe exposure are unresolved and valuation leaves little room.

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for CHRW. Reverse DCF needs about 11.7% 10-year FCF growth (9% discount rate, 3% terminal, fading) versus my base of about 10% fading, so the price asks for slightly more than base.

CHRW.scenario_basis: Start: FY2026E adjusted EPS $6.24 (Yahoo consensus, cross-check), price $147.10, dividend $2.52/yr. Base: EPS about $8.6 in Sep 2029 (+10%/yr), exit 20x, dividends about $8 over 3y. Bear: EPS $6.0, exit 15x, less about $3.8/share uninsured Lipe loss. Bull: EPS $11.0, exit 23x.

LYV.thesis_one_line: The world's biggest concert promoter and ticket seller keeps growing on record demand, but it lost a jury antitrust trial, may be forced to sell Ticketmaster, and the stock already prices flawless growth.
kill_criteria: Court enters equitable remedies in the Litigating States case requiring divestiture of Ticketmaster or sale of Live Nation-owned amphitheaters (docket order in the SDNY antitrust case, United States v. Live Nation).

Additional litigation accrual or judgment beyond the $450 million recorded in H1 2026 (10-Q Note 6, Corporate expenses) takes aggregate charges above $900 million in any subsequent filing, including any per-ticket damages calculation trebled under the Clayton Act.

Full-year 2026 consolidated adjusted operating income (non-GAAP, release reconciliation) grows less than 10% from 2025, contradicting 'on track for double-digit adjusted operating income growth this year' (Q2 2026 release).
Free cash flow - adjusted (company non-GAAP, release reconciliation) for full-year 2026 is below $1.3 billion, against $1,298.2 million in 2025, meaning growth capex is not converting.

Event-related deferred revenue at quarter-end (Q2 2026 record $6.4 billion, consolidated) grows less than 10% year over year at 30 Sep 2026 or 31 Dec 2026, signalling demand or sell-through has turned.
key_adverse_facts: 15 April 2026 jury verdict for the Litigating States on all remaining claims, with per-ticket damages (ticket count not yet set); states seek divestiture of Ticketmaster and sale of amphitheaters; remedies phase pending; post-trial motions argued 31 July 2026 (10-Q Note 6, filed 2026-07-30).

$450 million legal accrual recognised in H1 2026 (Corporate), plus a separate FTC and seven-state consumer-protection suit filed September 2025 with no accrual ('we do not believe that a loss is probable').

Consolidated debt principal $9,282.3 million at 30 Jun 2026 (10-Q debt table), of which $2,968.4 million is classified current, including the $1.0 billion 3.125% convertible notes (holder surrender window 1 Jul-30 Sep 2026) and $1.2 billion 6.5% secured notes due May 2027.

Live Nation stockholders' equity is only $82.3 million and 2025 GAAP diluted EPS was -$0.24; reported cash of $9.07 billion is largely client and event funds (company cites free cash of about $2 billion).
Concerts AOI fell 14% in Q2 2026 and is down 14% in H1; Q4 and Q1 are loss-making or weak quarters.
data_conflicts: Yahoo total cash $9.07 billion and EV $43.8 billion treat client and event cash as corporate cash; company states free cash of about $2 billion, so EV is about $48 billion on my bridge.
Yahoo forward P/E 90x and Q01 triage 134.7x NTM P/E rest on GAAP-like EPS distorted by NCI accretion and the legal accrual; I value on AOI and FCF - adjusted instead.
Q01 triage cited '33 states plus DC'; the 10-Q describes a settlement with the US and six further states, with the remaining Litigating States going to verdict.
LYV.next_earnings_date: 2026-11-04 (estimated from prior-year pattern, release of 2025-11-04; not confirmed)
LYV.confidence_in_thesis: low: the operating business is verified as strong, but the range of legal outcomes is wide and cannot be sized from filings.

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for LYV; triage also failed it. Reverse DCF on the generous FCF-adjusted base ($1.4 billion, before growth capex) needs about 15% 10-year growth versus my base of about 10%; after growth capex the requirement is far higher.

LYV.scenario_basis: Start: FCF-adjusted about $1.4B (2026E), price $170.87, about 245M diluted shares incl. converts, no dividend. Base: FCF-adj +10%/yr to about $1.86B, exit 28x, less $4/share further legal cost. Bear: FCF-adj $1.55B, 22x, less $10/share (forced remedies). Bull: $2.05B, 30x.

IR.thesis_one_line: A maker of industrial compressors and life-science pumps with strong cash conversion and a steady acquisition habit, but a full price for low single-digit organic growth.
kill_criteria: Organic revenue growth (release non-GAAP table, consolidated) is below 1% in two consecutive quarters, versus 2026 guidance of +1% to +3% organic growth.
Net debt to LTM adjusted EBITDA (company-reported, consolidated, release 'Balance Sheet and Cash Flow' paragraph) exceeds 2.5x, versus 1.7x at 30 Jun 2026.
Full-year 2026 adjusted EPS (non-GAAP, release) is reported below $3.45, the bottom of the current guidance range, or guidance is cut in any quarter.
Free cash flow to adjusted net income conversion (company definition) is below 85% for full-year 2026, against guidance of about 95% and 91% in 2025 ($1,220 million / $1,341 million).
IT&S segment adjusted EBITDA margin (release segment table) falls below 25.0% in any quarter outside Q1 seasonality, against 26.8% in Q2 2026 and 28.9% in Q4 2025.
key_adverse_facts: Organic growth is thin: 2026 guide is +1% to +3% organic and IT&S Q2 2026 organic orders were approximately flat; total revenue growth of 4.5%-6.5% leans on M&A (~2.5 points) and currency (~1 point).
IT&S segment adjusted EBITDA margin 26.8% in Q2 2026, down 180 bps year over year, from pricing not offsetting inflation in China and commercial investments.

Q2 2025 GAAP loss: $265.8 million goodwill and intangible impairments (Biopharma $170.3 million, Aerospace & Defense $59.4 million, tradename $36.1 million) plus a $120.9 million equity-method impairment; GAAP EPS TTM is $2.43 against adjusted $3.45.
Adjusted EPS adds back acquisition amortization (Q2 2026 $100.4 million pre-tax) and stock compensation ($17.8 million in Q2 2026); the 2026 adjusted EPS midpoint implies only +5% growth.

Q3 2026 will include a $162.5 million insurer settlement gain (ILC Dover) that flatters GAAP, not operations; $699.8 million 5.197% notes due June 2027 are classified current (consolidated debt table).
data_conflicts: Yahoo forward EPS $3.92 (likely FY2027 consensus) vs company FY2026 guide $3.45-$3.57: different years, but the 19.4x forward P/E embeds about +10% growth that is not in guidance.
Yahoo total debt $4,906.7 million vs 10-Q total long-term debt net $4,768.5 million carrying (Yahoo appears to include leases or other items); filing used.
b1 live rank 245 (composite 0.51) rests on value rank and weak momentum (-6.6% 12-1m); no triage entry found for IR in Q01/Q08 JSON.
IR.next_earnings_date: 2026-10-29 (estimated from prior-year pattern, release of 2025-10-30; not confirmed)
IR.confidence_in_thesis: med: cash conversion and balance sheet are verified; an organic growth inflection is unproven.

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for IR. Reverse DCF on $1.2 billion FCF needs about 11.7% 10-year growth versus my base of about 8% (EPS +7%/yr including buybacks).

IR.scenario_basis: Start: FY2026E adjusted EPS about $3.55 (guide $3.45-$3.57, high end), price $76.08, dividend $0.08/yr. Base: EPS about $4.6 in Sep 2029 (+7%/yr incl. buybacks), exit 20x. Bear: EPS $3.9, 16x. Bull: EPS $5.2, 23x.
